question.problem:
An inner product on $V={R}^{3}$ is defined as $⟨x,y⟩={x}_{1}{y}_{1}+4{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+7{x}_{3}{y}_{3}.$ 
Calculate the norm of the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ under this inner product.

current_example.problem:
An inner product on $V = \mathbb{R}^3$ is defined as $\langle \mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y} \rangle =  2x_1 y_1 + x_2 y_2 + 3x_3 y_3.$ 
Calculate the norm of the vector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14216488/assets/fc21d8c6daae3f193ecdd585d1705559f3746594b98908fcc531e89272cd7964.svg) under this inner product.
current_example.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $\mathbf v$ with respect to an inner product $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ is defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}‖v‖=\sqrt{⟨v,v⟩}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $\|\mathbf{v}\|$ using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}‖v‖ & =\sqrt{⟨v,v⟩} \\  & =\sqrt{2\cdot (3\cdot 3)+2\cdot 2+3\cdot (1\cdot 1)} \\  & =\sqrt{18+4+3} \\  & =\sqrt{25} \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$
